literal: Those who retaliated, as a thing of worth they will not esteem; they will treasure those who forbore, wrapping them up like gold.
translation: The wise will not esteem those who retaliate as worthy of any notice; but they will treasure those who patiently endure, wrapping them up like precious gold.
modern: தீமை செய்தவரைத் தண்டித்தவர்களை ஒரு பொருட்டாக மதிக்க மாட்டார்கள்; ஆனால், அத்தீமையைப் பொறுத்துக் கொண்டவர்களைப் பொன்னைப் போலப் போற்றி மனத்தில் வைப்பார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet contrasts how the world remembers those who take revenge versus those who practice forgiveness. The poet uses 'ஒறுத்தாரை' to denote those who retaliate, stating that they are not esteemed as anything of worth ('ஒன்றாக வையாரே'). In contrast, those who show forbearance ('பொறுத்தாரை') are highly valued. They are compared to 'பொன்' (gold), which is carefully wrapped ('பொதிந்து') and preserved as a treasure. True honor and lasting remembrance belong not to the vengeful, but to those who patiently endure wrongs.
